This project aims to develop an app which can
import data recorded from a race track session
and use AI to provide advice to the driver on
how to improve their lap times. This could
include advice on driving lines, braking, steering
and acceleration techniques as well as basic car
setup changes such as tyre pressures and
camber settings.

can include GPS position, speed, directions, G-forces

angles, tyre pressures and tyre temperature patterns.

others to provide insights into how the car is
performing and opportunities to improve the lap times.

Project ID: 2026-S2-08

Project title: Enhancing
Hospital Flow to
Improve Patient
Care and
Readmission
Outcomes

Sponsor: (SAS Institute
Inc.)

Brief description:
According to the Australian Medical
Association’s 2025 Public Hospital Report Card,
Australian hospitals face growing pressure from
rising demand, workforce constraints, limited
bed availability, and emergency department
congestion. Large volumes of administrative and
electronic health record (EHR) data are
collected, yet translating this information into
actionable insights remains challenging. SAS, a
global leader in analytics, supports more than
1,700 health and social services organisations
worldwide, helping improve patient outcomes
and operational efficiency. This highlights the
need for applied analytics approaches that
enable students to explore how data can
improve hospital workflows, patient outcomes,
and overall system efficiency.

Scope:
The project involves working with a de-identified
hospital dataset to investigate patient hospitalisation
patterns, readmissions, length of stay, and resource
utilisation using SAS analytics tools. Students will
undertake data preparation, cleaning, and
exploration, followed by exploratory and descriptive
analysis of patient and hospital activity to identify
patterns and factors associated with readmission risk
and length of stay. Where appropriate, the project
may include the development and evaluation of
predictive or statistical models, patient cohort
segmentation, and pathway analysis. Students will
communicate findings through dashboards,
visualisations, and written reports, develop
evidence-based recommendations supported by
analysis, and present outcomes to both academic and
industry stakeholders. As a student capstone project,
the emphasis is on applying analytical, teamwork,
communication, and problem-solving skills rather than
delivering production-ready solutions. Success will be
measured by the quality of the analysis, insights,
recommendations, and professional project delivery.

Skill requirements:
This project assumes that students have a
foundational level of technical and analytical
skills. Students should be comfortable with
data wrangling, including cleaning,
transforming, and working with structured
datasets such as hospital electronic health
records, and possess basic programming
skills, particularly in SAS (the primary tool),
with familiarity in Python, R, or SQL being
advantageous. The project also requires
competency in data visualisation to present
insights through dashboards and charts, as
well as an understanding of statistical
analysis and modelling, including descriptive
and diagnostic techniques to explore trends
and relationships. Additionally, some
exposure to predictive modelling, such as
regression or classification, is expected to
analyse outcomes like readmission risk or
length of stay, although more advanced
machine learning techniques are not
required. Overall, students should be able to
apply an end-to-end analytics workflow from
data preparation and exploration to
modelling and visualisation while
demonstrating critical thinking, problemsolving, and clear communication of insights.

Project ID: 2026-S2-09

Project title: Applied Sovereign
AI: Rapid
Prototyping MicroSaaS Solutions
with Agentaus

Sponsor: (Trellis Data)

Brief description:
The commercial technology sector is rapidly
shifting from building foundational AI models to
applying commercial APIs to solve niche, highvalue problems. However, integrating Large
Language Models (LLMs) into targeted
applications involves complex, infrequentlyencountered issues: mitigating AI hallucinations,
designing dynamic prompt architectures, and
ensuring data privacy.
This project operates as an "Applied AI
Innovation Sprint." Using Trellis Data’s
sovereign Agentaus API, student teams will be
tasked with identifying a specific, real-world
"micro-friction" (e.g., local business workflow
inefficiencies, student productivity bottlenecks,
or niche data processing tasks) and rapidly
prototyping a functional AI-driven application to
solve it.
Because the specific use-case is studentdefined, there is no obvious, standard-practice
solution. Students must engage in conceptual
thinking to define their own diverse stakeholder
needs, design an analytical approach to
evaluate AI output accuracy, and navigate the
conflicting technical constraints of time budgets
versus feature creep. This project provides
hands-on, enterprise-level experience with
commercial AI integration, bridging the gap
between theoretical computing and rapid market
deployment.

Scope:
Identify the high-level in-scope requirements and
activities of the project.
 Problem Scoping & System Analysis: Identifying a
specific, narrow user friction point (e.g., student
workflow, local retail data sorting) that can be solved
using an LLM.
 Prompt Engineering & Architecture: Designing,
testing, and refining dynamic prompts to ensure the
Agentaus API delivers accurate, contextually relevant,
and hallucination-free outputs.
 API Integration: Successfully connecting a
lightweight front-end or script to the Agentaus API via
standard REST/JSON protocols.
 Minimum Viable Product (MVP) Development:
Building a basic, functional user interface (Web app,
CLI, or simple dashboard) to interact with the AI
model.
 Evaluation & Testing: Developing an analytical
framework to test the AI's accuracy, latency, and
usability against the original problem statement.
 Agile Project Management: Delivering the prototype
within a strict 10-week (approx. 10-day effort) timebox
using agile sprints.

Skill requirements:
Identify the skillsets required of the project.
 Software Development / Coding:
Proficiency in Python or
JavaScript/TypeScript.
 API Integration: Experience or willingness
to learn RESTful APIs and JSON data
handling.
 Applied Artificial Intelligence: Basic
understanding of LLMs, prompt engineering,
and context window management.
 Web Development: Basic front-end skills
(HTML, CSS, React/Vue, or Python
frameworks like Streamlit/Flask) to build the
user interface.
 Business / System Analysis: Ability to
define user requirements and translate a
messy real-world problem into a logical
software architecture.
 Agile Project Management: Ability to
prioritise features, manage a tight time
budget, and execute weekly sprint
deliverables.

AI: Rapid
Prototyping MicroSaaS Solutions

Project ID: 2026-S2-11

Project title: CareSync: OfflineCapable Mobile
Logging for
Community Health
Field Visits

Sponsor: (Sri Ramakrishna
Engineering
College)

Brief description:
Community and home care workers regularly
visit clients in their homes, aged care facilities,
or remote/rural locations across the ACT and
surrounding NSW regions — many of which
have unreliable or no mobile connectivity.
Currently, visit notes, care task checklists, and
client observations are often recorded on paper
or in disconnected apps that require an active
internet connection, leading to delays, data loss,
and duplicated administrative work.
This project involves designing and developing a
mobile application that enables community
health and care workers to log client visits,
complete structured care checklists, record
observations and task completion, and capture
supporting notes — all while fully offline. Data
entered offline is securely queued on the device
and automatically synchronised with a central
system once connectivity is restored, with
conflict handling for cases where multiple
updates occur before syncing.

Scope:
1.Mobile application (Android and/or iOS) for care
workers to log client visits and complete care
checklists
2.Offline data capture: forms, checklists, and notes
can be filled in without an internet connection
3.Local on-device storage of unsynced data (e.g.
SQLite or equivalent local-first database)
4.Automatic background synchronisation to a central
server/database once connectivity is restored
5.Basic conflict handling for offline entries (e.g.
timestamp-based resolution, flagging conflicts for
review)
6.User authentication and role-based access (care
worker vs supervisor/admin)
7.Digital checklist builder or pre-configured checklist
templates (e.g. medication check, mobility support,
wellbeing 8.observation)Photo attachment support for
visit notes (optional, if relevant to sponsor's use case)
9.GPS/timestamp capture to verify visit location and
completion time
10.Simple web-based dashboard for supervisors to
view submitted visit logs and flag incomplete/overdue
visits
11.Basic data security measures (encrypted local
storage, secure transmission, login authentication)
12.Test/demo dataset using de-identified sample data
(no real client information)

Skill requirements:
Core Technical:
1.Mobile app development fundamentals
(Flutter/Dart or React Native/JavaScriptTypeScript)
2.Basic database concepts (SQL/NoSQL,
local vs. remote storage)
3.REST API design and consumption (or
willingness to learn Firebase/Supabase)
4.Version control (Git/GitHub) for team
collaboration
5.Basic UI/UX design principles for mobile
interfaces
Helpful but Not Essential:
1.Experience with offline-first or local-first
app architecture
2.Familiarity with cloud backend services
(Firebase, Supabase, AWS Amplify, or
similar)
3.Basic understanding of data
privacy/security principles (especially
relevant given health-related data)
4.Experience with state management in
mobile apps (Provider/Riverpod for Flutter,
Redux/Context API for React Native)

Project ID: 2026-S2-13

Project title: AI–Blockchain
Hybrid Intrusion
Detection System

Sponsor: (Sri Ramakrishna
Engineering
College)

Brief description:
Design and implement a hybrid Intrusion
Detection System (IDS) that combines a
machine learning/deep learning detection engine
with a blockchain layer for tamper-proof logging
and auditability. Every classification decision
(normal/attack, attack type, confidence score)
made by the AI model is hashed and recorded
on a blockchain ledger, ensuring the detection
history cannot be silently altered — even by an
insider with database access. This directly
extends existing hybrid ML/DL IDS work (e.g.,
ensemble or hybrid models like CNN-LSTM,
HMKELM-MTLBO-IDBSCAN) by adding a trust
and traceability layer.

Scope:
Training/evaluating ML/DL models (existing or new
hybrid models) on IDS datasets (e.g., CICIDS2017,
NSL-KDD, UNSW-NB15)
Designing a lightweight blockchain
(private/permissioned, e.g., Hyperledger Fabric or a
custom chain) for logging detection events
Smart contract logic for immutable event logging and
access control
Comparative performance evaluation: Accuracy,
Precision, Recall, F1-score, latency overhead with vs.
without blockchain logging
Visualization dashboard comparing model
performance across datasets

Skill requirements:
Python (scikit-learn, TensorFlow/PyTorch)
for ML/DL model development
Familiarity with IDS/network traffic datasets
and preprocessing
Blockchain basics: Hyperledger Fabric,
Ethereum (Solidity), or Ganache/Truffle for
prototyping
Smart contract development (Solidity) if
using Ethereum-based chain
Data visualization (Chart.js, Matplotlib, or
similar)
Basic understanding of consensus
mechanisms (PoW/PoA/PBFT)

Project title: AI-Powered Early
Autism Screening
and
Developmental
Support System

Sponsor: (Sri Ramakrishna
Engineering
College)

Brief description:
The project aims to develop an AI-powered early
autism screening and developmental support
system that identifies potential behavioral and
communication indicators associated with
Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD). The system
analyzes multimodal data such as facial
expressions, eye-gaze patterns, speech
characteristics, and behavioral interactions using
computer vision, natural language processing,
and deep learning techniques. It provides early
screening insights, developmental progress
tracking, and personalized activity
recommendations for children while maintaining
privacy, fairness, and ethical AI practices. The
proposed solution assists parents, educators,
and healthcare professionals in enabling timely
intervention and support, without replacing
clinical diagnosis.

Scope:
Collect and preprocess relevant child behavioral,
speech, video, and questionnaire-based datasets for
autism screening research.
Develop a multimodal AI pipeline combining video,
audio, and behavioral data analysis.
Implement computer vision techniques for analyzing
facial expressions, eye-gaze patterns, attention, and
interaction behaviors.
Develop speech and audio analysis modules to
identify communication patterns, speech delays, and
vocal characteristics.
Apply machine learning and deep learning models to
identify behavioral indicators associated with autism
spectrum characteristics.
Develop a risk assessment model that categorizes
developmental indicators into different levels (e.g.,
low concern, moderate concern, requires further
assessment).
Integrate standardized screening questionnaire data
to enhance AI-based assessment.
Develop a personalized recommendation module for
suggesting developmental activities and learning
support strategies.
Create a user-friendly web/mobile dashboard for
parents, caregivers, or educators to view assessment
insights and progress tracking.
Implement explainable AI techniques to improve
transparency of predictions.
Evaluate model performance using appropriate
metrics such as accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score,
and ROC-AUC.
Ensure ethical AI practices including child data
privacy, secure data handling, bias mitigation, and
responsible usage guidelines.

Skill requirements:
Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine
Learning (ML) concepts for developing
predictive models.
Deep Learning techniques for behavioral,
speech, and image-based analysis.
Computer Vision skills for facial expression
analysis, eye-gaze tracking, activity
recognition, and video processing.
Natural Language Processing (NLP) for
speech analysis, communication pattern
understanding, and text-based assessment.
Python Programming with libraries such as
NumPy, Pandas, OpenCV, Scikit-learn,

Brief description:
To advance Alzheimer’s diagnosis, we need to
combine diverse biomarkers with smart
computational tools. Agentic AI systems
autonomously analyze multimodal data including
cerebrospinal fluid proteins, plasma proteomics,
neuroimaging, and digital behavioral signals to
detect early pathological changes and predict
disease progression. These tools combine
machine learning with explainable frameworks,
improving clinical decision-making, reducing
diagnostic delays and allowing for customized
treatment strategies. In addition, ongoing
surveillance and digital phenotyping thru
wearables extend the range of biomarkers
beyond traditional laboratory measures. The
combination of agentic AI and biomarker science
promises earlier, more accurate and ethically
responsible detection of Alzheimer’s,
transforming patient care and accelerating
therapeutic development.

Scope:
The project requires defining biomarker selection,
establishing data integration pipelines, and deploying
agentic AI models. Activities include collecting
multimodal datasets (CSF, plasma, imaging, digital
signals), developing explainable AI frameworks,
validating outputs with clinical partners, and ensuring
ethical compliance. Continuous monitoring via
wearables and iterative model refinement are also in
scope. The project emphasizes early detection,
personalized progression tracking, and integration
into clinical workflows.

Skill requirements:
Students should be comfortable with
machine learning and data science, since
they’ll be designing predictive models and
working with complex biomarker datasets.
Bioinformatics skills are crucial for making
sense of proteomic and genomic data. On
the technical side, software development will
be needed to build pipelines and create
clinical dashboards. Finally, strong abilities in
business/system analysis and business
analytics will ensure the project stays aligned
with healthcare needs and delivers
meaningful outcomes.

Brief description:
For your capstone project, develop an anomaly
detection approach to identify irregularities in
real-world datasets, such as financial
transactions (e.g., fraudulent activities) or
healthcare data (e.g., abnormal patient vitals like
heart rate or blood pressure). You will collect
and preprocess cross-sectional or time series
data from public sources. Implement machine
learning models, such as Isolation Forest or
LSTM, to detect anomalies, evaluating their
performance using metrics like precision, recall,
and F1-score. Visualise detected anomalies and
patterns to provide actionable insights,
enhancing your skills in data analysis, machine
learning, and Python or R programming.
Optionally, deploy the model as a web-based
dashboard to showcase real-time anomaly
detection capabilities.
Out of Scope: Developing proprietary data
collection systems or hardware for real-time
financial or healthcare data acquisition.
 Implementing complex financial trading
platforms or clinical decision support systems
based on detected anomalies.
 Using paid or proprietary datasets requiring
subscriptions beyond freely available public
sources.
 Integrating with live external systems, such as
real-time banking platforms or hospital EHR
systems.

Scope:
 Data Collection: Gather time series or crosssectional data from reliable sources.
 Data Preprocessing: Clean and normalize data to
handle missing values, outliers, and ensure

positive rate to ensure accurate anomaly detection.

and trends.

performance, and insights in a detailed report for
clear communication of findings.

model implementation, and visualisation.

detection techniques (e.g., Isolation Forest,

Project ID: 2026-S2-24

Project title: Simulating
Autonomous
Robot Swarms

Sponsor: (Essam Debie)

Brief description:
Want to create the world a robot swarm lives in
and the intelligence that drives it? Join our
capstone project to build a Python-based
simulation environment and program a swarm of
autonomous robots that navigate, coordinate,
and complete missions together, no human
control needed. Your work will directly power a
research study on how people supervise robotic
swarms. This is your chance to level up your
coding skills and work on something that could
shape the future of robotics!

Scope:
You will develop two tightly connected pieces: the
environment and the swarm that operates inside it:
1. The Simulation Environment
A configurable 2D operational area with obstacles,
waypoints, and task zones (e.g., search areas,
delivery points, inspection targets).
Scenario configuration via simple files (JSON) so
researchers can change layouts, mission types, and
difficulty without touching code.
Environmental dynamics such as moving obstacles or
changing task locations to keep the swarm
challenged.
2. The Swarm
Swarm behaviours that run on their own: flocking
(separation, alignment, cohesion), formation keeping,
and collision avoidance.
Task allocation: the swarm autonomously divides up
work such as area coverage, target search, and pointto-point delivery.
Imperfect agents: individual robots can drift off
course, drop out, or misreport status creating realistic
events for a human supervisor to catch.
You will add controls to scale the swarm size and
adjust behaviour parameters (speed, spacing,
autonomy level), build a dashboard to visualise the
swarm in action, and stream task and swarm-state
data (timestamped logs) to an external system for
analysis (not part of the project). Your work will help
researchers study how humans monitor and intervene
in swarm operations during a pilot study.

Skill requirements:
Python programming

Grasping in

Sponsor: (Xing Wang)

Brief description:
The goal of this project is to reproduce the
ThinkGrasp pipeline, a state-of-the-art robotic
grasping system that uses Vision-Language
Models (VLMs) to reason about and grasp
objects in heavily cluttered environments. While
the original paper relies on the commercial GPT4o API, this student project will focus on
reproducing the simulation environment and
attempting to replace the costly closed-source
model with open-source alternatives (e.g.,
LLaVA, Qwen-VL) to achieve a more accessible
and autonomous system. The system will
interpret natural language commands (e.g.,
"Pick up the red apple under the box") and
execute multi-step manipulation (removing
obstacles first).

Scope:
Pipeline Reproduction (Existing Resources):
1. Deploy the official ThinkGrasp code (Open
Source).
2. Integrate the segmentation module (LangSAM /
VLPart) and grasp generation module (GraspNet or
similar) as described in the paper.
3. Set up the simulation environment (likely PyBullet
or Isaac Gym) to replicate the "cluttered desk"
scenarios.
Model Substitution (New Challenge):
1. Replace the reasoning core (GPT-4o) with an
open-source VLM (e.g., LLaVA-Next, Qwen-VL-Chat,
or DeepSeek-VL) to evaluate if smaller, local models
can handle the "strategic reasoning" required for
removing obstacles.
Performance Benchmarking:
1. Compare the success rate (Success Rate) and
planning time between the GPT-4o version and the
open-source VLM version.

Skill requirements:
Deep Learning & NLP: Experience with
PyTorch and huggingface transformers
library; understanding of how to prompt and
inference Large Language Models
(LLMs/VLMs).
Computer Vision: Understanding of object
detection, segmentation masks
Robotics & Simulation

properties: Seal (airtightness) and Wrench
(resistance to gravity/torque). Students will
utilize the SuctionNet-1Billion dataset to
investigate how different fine-tuning strategies
(e.g., Layer Freezing, Differential Learning
Rates, or Loss re-weighting) affect a model's
ability to learn these physical constraints. The
goal is to determine the optimal training recipe
that allows a standard vision backbone (e.g.,
ResNet-50 or ViT) to generalize to unseen,
cluttered 3D objects in simulation.

Scope:
Backbone Pre-training Analysis: Compare the starting
point efficacy: ImageNet pre-trained weights vs.
PointNet (geometric) pre-trained weights.
Fine-tuning Experimentation:
Layer-wise Analysis: Systematically freeze different
stages of the backbone to determine which layers
capture the "surface geometry" required for suction.
Loss Function Engineering: Design and fine-tune a
composite loss function that balances classification
(Suctionable or not) and regression (Seal/Wrench
scores), addressing the data imbalance problem.
Hyperparameter Sweeping: rigorous testing of
learning rate schedulers (Cosine Annealing vs. Step
Decay) to optimize convergence speed and final
accuracy.
Simulation-based Evaluation: Use the SuctionNet
simulation API to run inference on the test set and
generate heatmaps. Evaluation is purely metricbased: Mean Perfection Rate (MPR) and Success
Rate at different error tolerances.

Skill requirements:
Deep Learning Theory: Deep understanding
of Backpropagation, Overfitting,
Regularization, and Transfer Learning
mechanisms.
PyTorch/TensorFlow: Ability to write custom
training loops, custom Loss functions, and
use hooks to visualize gradients.
Experiment Tracking: Proficiency with tools
like Weights & Biases (WandB) or
TensorBoard to visualize loss curves and
compare dozens of training runs.
Data Analysis: Ability to analyze confusion
matrices and regression error distributions to
diagnose "why the model failed."
documents.title:
Fine-Tuning
Strategies for
Physics-Aware
Suction Grasping:
A Data-Centric
Simulation Study

Project ID: 2026-S2-35

Project title: Interactive AgriVision: One-Click
Panoptic
Segmentation for
Complex Crop
Monitoring

Sponsor: (Xing.wang;
Shuangzhe.liu;
Min.wang)

Brief description:
This project aims to develop or reproduce a
Panoptic One-Click Segmentation framework
specifically tailored for unstructured agricultural
environments. While current Foundation Models
(like SAM) excel at instance segmentation
("things" like fruits), they often struggle with
semantic regions ("stuff" like ground, sky, or
dense foliage) in a unified workflow. This project
will implement a model that accepts sparse user
prompts (single clicks) to segment both crop
instances and environmental background
simultaneously. The goal is to drastically reduce
the data annotation time for agricultural datasets
and enable "human-in-the-loop" visual reasoning
for orchard robots

Scope:
Model Architecture: Implement a panoptic
segmentation network (e.g., combining a
Mask2Former or Panoptic-DeepLab backbone)
integrated with an interactive Prompt Encoder (similar
to SAM) to handle click inputs.
Agricultural Adaptation: Fine-tune or train the model
on agricultural datasets (e.g., MinneApple, CVPPP, or
SugarBeets) to handle specific challenges like
occlusion, variable lighting, and clustered fruits.
Interaction Logic: Develop a logic layer that
distinguishes whether a user's click intends to select a
discrete object (fruit) or a continuous region
(foliage/ground) based on feature extraction.
Evaluation: Measure performance using Panoptic
Quality (PQ) metrics and Number of Clicks (NoC)
required to reach a target Intersection over Union
(IoU) of 85%+.

Skill requirements:
Deep Learning & Computer Vision:
proficiency in PyTorch;
Interactive AI: Understanding of prompt
engineering for vision models and loss
functions for semi-supervised or weaklysupervised learning.
Data Handling: Experience with COCOformat datasets and conversion tools for
panoptic annotations.
UI/Visualization: Ability to build a simple
interactive demo (using Gradio, Streamlit, or
OpenCV) to visualize the "Click -> Segment"
process in real-time.

Project ID: 2026-S2-36

Project title: Explicit Truss
Structure
Parametrisation
for Soft Robotic
Grippers

Sponsor: (Xing Wang,
Damith Herath,
Min.Wang)

Brief description:
This project focuses on the explicit
computational design of Additive Manufacturing
(AM) structures for soft robotics. Rather than
relying on complex implicit mathematical fields,
this project restricts the design representation
strictly to explicit 3D truss structures (defined
networks of nodes and struts) to govern the
compliance and kinematics of a soft robotic
gripper. By parametrising the macro-geometry of
these explicit lattices, designers can directly
encode structural constraints for Fused
Deposition Modelling (FDM). This
straightforward approach aims to significantly
reduce costly trial-and-error iterations during
physical 3D printing

Scope:
Parametric generation and explicit 3D modelling of
truss and lattice structures tailored for soft-robot
morphology.
Physical additive manufacturing validation using
highly flexible 3D printing filaments, specifically TPU.
Delivery and experimental testing of a physical soft
robotic gripper within an automated grasping pipeline

Skill requirements:
CAD design, e.g. SolidWorks;
Computational Design: Proficiency in
parametric CAD tools (e.g., Grasshopper,
Python API) to explicitly model 3D truss
networks and define precise geometrical
constraints.
Python

Project ID: 2026-S2-41

Project title: Critical Thinking’s
Resilience in the
Age of Generative
AI in Higher
Education

Sponsor: (Ahmed Imran)

Brief description:
Over a century ago, the German philosopher
Emanuel Kant defined universities as institutions
dedicated to reasoning. Since then, universities
have evolved, influenced by technological
advancements and socio-economic challenges.
Despite these changes, critical thinking remains
a fundamental attribute and an essential skill for
graduates. There are increasing concerns that
the rapid development of generative artificial
intelligence (Gen AI) may significantly impact
this aspect. Existing literature has examined this
phenomenon from various perspectives and with
diverse methodologies yet often fails to clearly
establish or articulate the relationship through
multiple disciplinary lenses, including
neuroscience, psychology, and information
science. This project aims to develop a
conceptual framework for the key components
by decomposing each factor into measurable
and well-defined instruments within the context
of higher education.

Scope:
 Extensive literature review of highly relevant
academic articles
 Establish the critical relationship of key
constructs/ sub constructs through chain of
evidence and examples from extant literature.
 Demonstration of rigor through application of
appropriate methodology, logical progression of
arguments and evidence

Skill requirements:
 Good exposure to research
methodology, particularly qualitative
research, literature review technique
 Good writing ability
 Critical thinking and ability to synthesize
and interpret complex data.

Resilience in the

AI in Higher

Distraction
Detection Using

al and EyeTracking Signals

Sponsor: (Ghazal
Bargshady)

Brief description:
This project investigates how different sensing
modalities contribute to driver distraction
detection. Students will critically review studies
using physiological signals (ECG, GSR, EEG,
fNIRS), eye movements, facial behaviour, and
vehicle dynamics, comparing their advantages,
limitations, and suitability for real-world
deployment. The outcome will be a
comprehensive review paper highlighting
challenges and opportunities for multimodal
driver monitoring.

Scope:
Conduct a comprehensive literature review on AIbased driver distraction detection.
Review and compare different types of driver
distraction, including cognitive, visual, auditory, and
manual distraction.
Investigate sensing modalities used in driver
monitoring systems, such as computer vision, eye
tracking, physiological signals (ECG, GSR),
neurological signals (EEG/fNIRS), and vehicle
kinematic data.
Critically analyse machine learning and deep learning
approaches reported in the literature.
Compare publicly available driver distraction datasets,
experimental protocols, and evaluation metrics.
Identify current research challenges, limitations, and
gaps in multimodal driver distraction detection.
Propose future research directions and
recommendations for developing robust, explainable,
and real-world AI-based driver monitoring systems.
Prepare a conference-style research paper
summarising the findings and proposed future work.

and Machine Learning concepts.
Knowledge of data analytics and
fundamental data science principles.

findings.
Strong academic writing and technical
communication skills.
Ability to organise information, analyse
research trends, and present findings clearly.
Experience with Microsoft Word, Excel, and
presentation software.
Basic project management and time
management skills.

Brief description:
This project explores the use of Large Language
Models (LLMs) combined with a Generative
behaviour planner (Fabric/GPSFSM) to achieve
autonomous robotic exploration without relying
on dedicated frontier exploration software.
Students will set up an environment using the
TurtleBot 4 platform, leveraging existing ROS 2
generic navigation (Nav2) and image analysis
capabilities. The LLM will act as a high-level
cognitive engine orchestrating exploration
strategies. The performance of this LLM-driven
approach will be compared against traditional
frontier-based exploration methods (like
explore_lite), culminating in a research paper
targeting robotics conferences such as ACRA.

Scope:
- Setting up a physical or simulated evaluation arena.
- Deploying the ROS2 based software stack on a
TurtleBot 4.
- Experimenting and fine-tuning behaviour plans to
implement exploration based on available skills.
- Running comparative benchmarks against traditional
frontier exploration.
- Writing a paper for ACRA with the results

- ROS 2 (Robot Operating System),
- Python/C++ Programming, -
- Prompt Engineering/LLM integration,
- Linux basics,

Brief description:
As robots operate in crowded social spaces,
determining which humans intend to interact
with the robot is challenging. This project
develops a vision-based pipeline operating from
the robot's point-of-view to identify and filter out
bystanders versus potential interaction partners.
Students will utilize object identification, skeleton
tracking, and head pose/gaze estimation to
assess human attention toward the robot. The
system will be mounted on a physical robot
platform and validated under real-world humanrobot interaction scenarios. The ultimate goal is
to build an efficient, deployable perception
module and produce a research publication for
ACRA.

Scope:
- Developing a vision pipeline using existing models
(e.g., YOLO, OpenPose, MediaPipe) for object and
skeleton detection.
- Implementing gaze and face orientation estimation.
- Defining a filtering algorithm to classify interactable
humans based on tracking data.
- Deployment and testing on standard camera
hardware.

Skill requirements:
- Computer Vision,
- Machine Learning,

Brief description:
In dynamic environments, people might
approach a robot from outside its main field of
vision. This project aims to create an audiodriven human interaction detection system.
Utilising a microphone array or multiple
independent microphones, students will
implement Sound Source Localisation (SSL) and
Direction of Arrival (DoA) algorithms to detect
where sounds originate relative to the robot. The
pipeline will also incorporate localised speechto-text to identify if the speaker is specifically
addressing the robot, allowing the robot to orient
its camera stack appropriately. The outcome will
be a hardware/software combined module and
an ACRA paper submission.

Scope:
- Implementing Direction of Arrival (DoA) algorithms
for a multi-microphone setup (e.g., using ODAS).
- Integrating Speech-to-Text (STT) and Wake-word
detection systems.
- Filtering background noise and third-party
conversations.
- Sending orientation commands to the robot
base/camera based on acoustic data.

Skill requirements:
- Audio Signal Processing,
- Python/C++,
- ROS 2,
- Embedded Systems,
- Basic Machine Learning (for STT
integration).

Project title: PII Scrubber for
Long-term Robotic
Data Logging

Sponsor: (Kalana
Ratnayake

Brief description:
Robots operating in public environments
frequently record Personally Identifiable
Information (PII) such as faces and voices. For
long-term human-robot interaction, robots must
retain identity context while adhering to privacy
requirements. This project develops a PII
scrubber tool tailored for robotic datasets. The
system will de-identify facial and conversational
information before storage, while maintaining an
encrypted or tokenised secondary database that
allows authorised contextual retrieval when
interacting with the same humans later. The
deliverable is an open-source Python package
functioning seamlessly alongside robot
databases, aiming for an ACRA publication.

Scope:
- Developing a Python package to detect
and obfuscate (blur/tokenize) faces and PII in data
streams.
- Implementing a database (SQLite) wrapper for
linking anonymised data with collected data, such as
conversational text, for storage and retrieval.
- Evaluating the performance and latency of the
scrubbing process during standard operations.

Skill requirements:
- Python,
- Data Privacy & Security principles,
- Database Management (SQL/NoSQL),
- Computer Vision, Audio and STT

Project ID: 2026-S2-48

Project title: An AI Enabled
Shared Family
Shopping App
designed for Older
Adults

Sponsor: (Blooma John)

Brief description:
This project aims to develop an AI-enabled
shared family shopping application that supports
older adults, including those experiencing mild
cognitive impairment (MCI), in managing
everyday grocery shopping. The app allows
family members to collaboratively create,
update, and monitor shopping lists in real time
while providing intelligent memory-support
features such as personalized reminders,
frequently purchased item suggestions, voice
interaction, and shopping history tracking.
Designed using age-friendly and cognitively
accessible principles, the application prioritizes
simplicity, readability, and ease of use. The goal
is to enhance independence, reduce cognitive
burden, strengthen family support, and improve
the overall shopping experience for older adults.

Scope:
The project will include the design and development
of a shared, cloud-based grocery shopping
application that provides real-time synchronization of
shopping lists across multiple devices and users
within a household. Key functionality includes:
User registration, login, and household/group
management.
Creation of new shopping lists and modification of
existing lists.
Real-time synchronization of list data across
smartphones, tablets, and web interfaces.
Shared access for multiple household members.
Add, edit, delete, and update grocery items.
Search and filter grocery items within a list.
Sort items by category, name, status, assigned user,
or favorites.
Mark items as purchased or pending.
Assign categories (e.g., fruit, vegetables, dairy,
cleaning products).
Record item details including quantity, unit of
measure, preferred brand, notes, and favorite status.
Assign responsibility for purchasing specific items to
nominated household members.
Basic settings management (profile, notifications,
accessibility preferences).
Support for touch-based interaction on mobile and
tablet devices.
Text-based input for item entry and list management.
Voice-enabled item entry and voice commands were
supported by the device platform.
AI-assisted features such as frequently purchased
item suggestions, shopping reminders, and intelligent
list recommendations.
Accessibility features designed for older adults,
including large text, simple navigation, high-contrast
display options, and intuitive user interfaces.
Secure cloud storage and backup of shopping lists
and user preferences.
This scope focuses on supporting collaborative
household shopping, improving accessibility for older
adults, and providing AI-enabled assistance to reduce
memory burden and enhance independence.

Skill requirements:
Mobile and Web Application Development
Database and Cloud Services (including
real-time synchronisation)
AI and Voice Technology Integration
User Interface (UI) Design
User Experience (UX) and Accessibility
Design
Human-Computer Interaction (HCI) for Older
Adults and MCI Users
Requirements Analysis and Stakeholder
Engagement
Agile Project Management
Software Testing and Quality Assurance

Project ID: 2026-S2-49

Project title: Cognitive
Workload in
Multiple Tasks

Sponsor: (Raul FernandezRojas)

Brief description:
The Cognitive Workload in Multiple Tasks
project focuses on understanding and modelling
the mental effort required when individuals
perform multiple tasks. The project aims to
develop computational and machine learning
models capable of assessing cognitive workload
and predicting performance under varying task
demands. By identifying patterns associated
with workload fluctuations, the research seeks to
enhance the design of intelligent, humancentred systems that can adapt to users'
cognitive states. The outcomes of this project
will contribute to improved decision-making,
productivity, safety, and user experience across
a range of operational and technology-driven
domains.

Scope:
The project will include the following high-level
requirements and activities:
Review and analyse existing literature on cognitive
workload, multitasking, and human performance.
Define cognitive workload indicators and performance
measures relevant to multiple-task environments.
Conduct data collection activities to capture
behavioural, physiological, and task performance data
associated with cognitive workload.
Design and implement methodologies for cognitive
workload assessment and modelling.
Develop computational and machine learning models
to estimate, classify, and predict cognitive workload
levels.

Skill requirements:
Students interested in this project should
have a combination of technical, analytical,
and research skills. The following skillsets
are desirable:
Programming and Software Development
(e.g., Python, MATLAB, R, or similar
programming languages).
Data Analytics and Data Science including
data preprocessing, feature engineering,
statistical analysis, and data visualisation.
Problem Solving and Critical Thinking to
analyse complex research questions and
develop innovative solutions.
Technical Documentation and Scientific
Writing for reporting findings and preparing
publications or project documentation.
Project Management and Teamwork Skills to
support effective collaboration, planning, and
delivery of project milestones.

how cognitive workload changes when

human performance in immersive environments
and support the design of adaptive VR systems
that enhance training effectiveness, user
experience, and operational performance.

requirements and activities:
Review and analyse literature related to cognitive
workload, virtual reality, and human performance.
Collect behavioural, physiological, and task
performance data during VR task execution.
Investigate the impact of task complexity and
environmental factors on cognitive workload.
Develop methodologies for cognitive workload
assessment within VR environments.
Analyse the relationship between cognitive workload,
user performance, and VR interaction.
Document findings through reports, publications, and
presentations.

Project ID: 2026-S2-54

Project title: Development of a
Modular CableDriven Serial
Elastic Structure
with ROS2
Middleware
Interface
Compliance

Sponsor: (Maleen
Jayasuriya)

Brief description:
The Collaborative Robotics Lab's RAPP Lab
programme explores human-robot interaction
through physical theatre, treating robots as
creative ensemble members rather than tools.
Current work uses rigid-link industrial cobots.
This project asks what a fundamentally different
morphology brings to the stage. Students will
design, fabricate and control a servo-actuated,
tendon-driven continuum arm at the scale of a
collaborative robot arm (approximately 900 mm
reach). The arm must be fully modular: designed
for repeated disassembly, transport and
reassembly between studio and performance
venues. Deliverables include the physical
platform, a ROS2 control stack, and complete
assembly documentation.

Scope:
1. Mechanical design and CAD modelling of a multisegment, tendon-driven continuum arm at cobot
scale, with payload treated as a secondary
consideration
2. A modular architecture in which every segment can
be disassembled and reassembled with standard
tools, verified through repeated teardown and rebuild
cycles
3. Fabrication using accessible methods (3D printing,
laser cutting, off the shelf servos and hardware)
4. Servo actuation electronics and embedded control,
including cable tensioning and routing
5. A ROS2 (Humble) control stack exposing a
standard joint-space command interface using ROS2
Moveit, with basic open-loop control based on
constant-curvature kinematic assumptions
6. Scripted and teleoperated (through Xbox controller)
motion demonstrations suitable for a live performance
context, including basic safety behaviours (velocity
limiting, soft stops, e-stop)
7. Complete technical documentation: assembly and
disassembly guide, wiring diagrams, bill of materials,
and software setup instructions
8. Design for forward compatibility: the command
interface must be structured so that a learned motion
model could drive the arm in future work using ROS2
Moveit

Skill requirements:
1. At least one member having prior
participation in a RAPP Lab workshop or
project (essential). The arm is being built for
a live performance research context, and
familiarity with the lab's working methods,
safety culture and studio environment is a
prerequisite. Applicants without this
background will not be considered.
2. Working ROS2 knowledge (essential):
comfortable writing and debugging ROS2
and Moveit nodes in Python, using topics,
services, launch files and parameters, and
interfacing ROS2 with hardware over serial
or a servo bus. This is not a learn-as-you-go
requirement; applicants should be able to
point to prior ROS2 work.
3. Hardware modelling and mechanical
design (essential): proficiency in parametric
CAD (Fusion 360, SolidWorks or similar),
design for 3D printing and laser cutting, and
tolerance-aware design for parts that must
survive repeated assembly and disassembly.
4. Embedded and electronics competence:
microcontroller programming, servo control
(PWM or a bus protocol such as Dynamixel),
wiring and power budgeting.
5. Mathematical maturity: willingness to
engage with continuum kinematics (constantcurvature models) at the level of
implementing them in code.
6. Version control and documentation
discipline: all design files and code under Git,
with documentation treated as a first-class
deliverable rather than an afterthought.
Team roles will span mechanical, electronics
and software streams, but every team
member is expected to meet the ROS2 and
RAPP Lab criteria.

Project ID: 2026-S2-56

Project title: Advanced
Machine Learning
Models for Robust
sEMG Gesture
Recognition and
Robotic Hand
Control

Sponsor: (Xing wang)

Brief description:
This project focuses on the core machine
learning and data science challenges of using
surface electromyography (sEMG) for humanrobot interaction.
Biomedical signals like sEMG are notoriously
noisy and suffer from significant cross-subject
variance and muscle fatigue degradation.
Rather than focusing on hardware, students will
focus on developing and optimising advanced
machine learning and deep learning models
(e.g., CNNs, LSTMs, or Attention mechanisms)
to achieve highly accurate and generalisable
gesture classification.
The project emphasises high-dimensional
feature engineering, domain adaptation (transfer
learning across different users - stretch goal),
and optimising models for real-time inference
latency.
The final optimised algorithms will be deployed
to drive a physical robotic hand, demonstrating
the practical robustness of the developed
models.

Scope:
Advanced Feature Representation: Implementing
time-frequency feature extraction (e.g., Wavelet
Transforms, Spectrograms) and applying
dimensionality reduction techniques (e.g., PCA, tSNE) to process high-dimensional multi-channel data.
Deep Learning Model Development: Designing,
training, and tuning advanced neural network
architectures tailored for time-series physiological
data, comparing them against classical baselines
(SVM, Random Forest).
Cross-Subject Generalisation: Investigating transfer
learning, few-shot learning, or domain adaptation
techniques to improve model accuracy on new,
unseen users without requiring extensive recalibration
datasets.
Real-Time Inference Optimisation: Profiling and
optimising the trained models (e.g., through
quantisation or efficient sliding-window architectures)
to ensure low-latency, real-time prediction stability.
System Deployment: Integrating the optimised
machine learning pipeline with a basic communication
interface to actuate a physical robotic hand based on
live gesture predictions.

Skill requirements:
Advanced Machine Learning & Deep
Learning: Strong proficiency in Python and
deep learning frameworks (PyTorch or
TensorFlow), with an understanding of
sequence modelling and neural network
optimisation.
Data Science & Analytics: Expertise in
handling noisy time-series datasets,
statistical performance evaluation (e.g., kfold cross-validation, precision-recall
analysis), and managing class imbalances.
MLOps & Deployment: Understanding of
real-time algorithmic pipelines, decision
smoothing logic (e.g., majority voting,
confidence thresholding), and translating
offline models to online inference.
Basic System Integration: Ability to interface
Python-based predictive models with
external hardware via standard
communication protocols (e.g., Serial, UDP,
or basic ROS2 wrappers).

Project ID: 2026-S2-57

Project title: Decoding Visual
Perception from
Brain Signals
using Deep
Learning

Sponsor: (Min Wang)

Brief description:
Brain-computer interfaces (BCIs) enable
communication between the human brain and
computers by interpreting neural activity. Recent
advances have demonstrated the possibility of
reconstructing visual experiences directly from
electroencephalography (EEG) signals. This
project aims to develop a prototype system that
decodes dynamic visual information from EEG
recordings using deep learning techniques.
Students will utilise a publicly available dataset
and investigate temporal neural representations
for predicting video content or semantic
attributes from EEG signals. The project
combines machine learning, computer vision,
signal processing and generative AI, providing
practical experience in developing intelligent
neuro-inspired systems for next-generation
human-computer interaction applications.

Scope:
Expected Deliverables:
-Literature review on EEG-based visual perception
decoding and brain–computer interfaces.
-A project report written in research paper style that
includes:
(1) Whole processing pipeline and system
architecture.
(2) Deep learning model for decoding visual
information from EEG signals (e.g., object category,
scene type, or semantic attributes).
(3) Performance evaluation against baseline machine
learning or deep learning models using standard
evaluation metrics.
(4) Visualisation and analysis of decoded visual
representations and model performance.
(5) This final project report should describe the
methodology, experimental results, limitations, and
future work.
-Well-documented source code.
-A prototype demonstrating EEG-based visual
perception decoding.
The project will include the following high-level
requirements and activities:
-Review literature on EEG-based visual decoding and
brain-computer interfaces.
-Install and configure the development environment.
-Obtain and preprocess a publicly available EEG
dataset.
-Perform EEG preprocessing, including filtering,
normalization, and segmentation.
-Extract temporal/spectral EEG representations using
deep learning models.
-Implement one or more baseline neural decoding
models.
-Predict semantic information (e.g., object category,
motion, colour) from EEG signals.
-Evaluate model performance using suitable metrics.
-Visualise learned EEG representations and
prediction results.
-Compare experimental results with published
baseline models.
-Produce technical documentation and a
demonstration of the developed prototype.

Skill requirements:
This project involves massive programming
and deep learning. It is suitable for students
who have a solid background in Machine
Learning.
Essential:
-Python programming
-Machine Learning fundamentals
-Deep Learning (PyTorch preferred)
-GPU programming (CUDA)
-Basic signal processing
-Data analysis and visualisation
-Git version control
Desirable
-Computer Vision
-Time-series analysis
-EEG signal processing
-Transformers or sequence models
-Experience with PyTorch Lightning or
HuggingFace
-Basic knowledge of Brain-Computer
Interfaces (BCI)

Project ID: 2026-S2-58

Project title: EmoSens:
Multimodal
Emotion
Recognition using
EEG and
Physiological
Signals

Sponsor: (Min Wang)

Brief description:
Emotion recognition plays an increasingly
important role in intelligent human-computer
interaction, healthcare, education, and
collaborative robotics. While facial expressions
and speech are commonly used for emotion
recognition, physiological signals such as
electroencephalography (EEG),
electrocardiography (ECG), and electrodermal
activity (EDA) provide objective measures of a
person's internal emotional state. This project
aims to develop a multimodal deep learning
system that integrates EEG with complementary
physiological or behavioural signals to improve
emotion recognition accuracy and robustness.
Students will investigate multimodal data fusion
techniques and evaluate machine learning
models using publicly available datasets,
contributing to the development of more
adaptive and human-centred intelligent systems.

Scope:
Expected Deliverables:
-Literature review on multimodal emotion recognition
-A report in research paper style that includes:
(1) Physiological signal preprocessing pipeline
(2) Baseline unimodal emotion recognition models
(3) Multimodal fusion framework
(4) Experimental comparison of fusion strategies
(5) Performance evaluation using standard metrics
-Source code with documentation
-A demonstration
The project will include the following high-level
requirements and activities:
-Conduct a literature review on affective computing
and multimodal emotion recognition.
-Select and study one or more public emotion
recognition datasets (e.g., DEAP, MAHNOB-HCI,
SEED-IV, SEED-V).
-Preprocess EEG signals and additional modalities
such as ECG, EDA, facial expressions, eye gaze, or
respiration.
-Extract features using signal processing and deep
learning techniques.
-Develop unimodal baseline emotion recognition
models.
-Design and implement multimodal fusion strategies
(early fusion, late fusion, or attention-based fusion).
-Train and evaluate deep learning models for emotion
classification.
-Compare different modality combinations and fusion
methods.
-Visualise learned feature representations and model
predictions.
-Document the developed system and experimental
findings.

Skill requirements:
Essential:
-Python programming
-Machine Learning fundamentals
-Deep Learning (PyTorch or TensorFlow)
-Data preprocessing and visualisation
-Basic signal processing
-Git version control
Desirable:
-EEG signal analysis

PPG)
-Computer Vision (for facial expression
recognition)
-Multimodal deep learning
-Attention mechanisms and Transformers

Sponsor: (Min Wang; Xing

Brief description:
Multimodal physiological sensing is increasingly
used in human–computer interaction, affective
computing, and brain–computer interface
research. However, collecting synchronised data
from multiple sensing devices often requires
substantial software development and
integration. This project aims to develop a
unified multimodal data acquisition platform
capable of simultaneously collecting
electroencephalography (EEG),
electrocardiography (ECG), electrodermal
activity (GSR), and webcam-based eye-tracking
data. The platform will provide real-time signal
acquisition, stream synchronisation,
preprocessing, visualisation, data storage, and
an intuitive graphical user interface. The
completed system will serve as a reusable
research platform for future multimodal sensing
and artificial intelligence studies.

supporting EEG, ECG, GSR, and webcam-based eye
tracking.

multiple sensor streams.
-Signal preprocessing modules for filtering,
normalisation, and basic artefact removal.
-Interactive graphical user interface for experiment
control and device management.

signals.
-Data recording system with synchronised
timestamps and experiment metadata.
-Software architecture documentation and user
manual.

acquisition and recording.

implementation, testing, and future extensions.
The project will include the following high-level
requirements and activities:

sensing platforms and communication protocols.

from EEG, ECG, GSR, and webcam-based eyetracking devices.

monitoring, and recording control.

Project ID: 2026-S2-60

Project title: Learning Emotion
Transition
Patterns from
EEG Signals
using Graph
Neural Networks

Sponsor: (Min Wang)

Brief description:
Emotions are dynamic processes that evolve
continuously over time rather than occurring as
isolated states. Conventional EEG-based
emotion recognition methods typically classify
each time segment independently, overlooking
temporal dependencies between emotional
states. This project aims to develop a graph
neural network (GNN) framework to learn
emotion transition patterns directly from EEG
signals. The project will evaluate whether graphbased temporal modelling improves emotion
recognition accuracy, robustness, and
interpretability compared with conventional deep
learning approaches.

Scope:
Expected Deliverables:
-Literature review
-EEG preprocessing pipeline
-Temporal graph construction module
-Graph neural network implementation
-Experimental comparison with baseline methods
-Visualisation of learned emotion transition patterns
-Source code with documentation
-Final report and project demonstration
The project will include the following high-level
requirements and activities:
-Conduct a literature review on EEG-based emotion
recognition and graph neural networks.
-Select and preprocess a publicly available EEG
emotion dataset (e.g., DEAP, SEED-IV, or SEED-V).
-Perform EEG preprocessing, including filtering,
segmentation, and normalisation.
-Extract EEG features using conventional signal
processing or deep learning techniques.
-Construct temporal graphs from sequential EEG
segments.
-Implement a Graph Neural Network (e.g., GCN or
Graph Attention Network) to model temporal
dependencies.
-Compare the proposed model against baseline
methods such as CNNs, LSTMs, or Transformers.
-Evaluate performance using standard emotion
recognition metrics.
-Visualise learned emotion transition patterns and
graph attention weights.
-Develop a demonstration system and technical
documentation.

Skill requirements:
Essential:
-Python programming
-Machine Learning fundamentals
-Deep Learning (PyTorch preferred)
-Data analysis and visualisation
-Basic signal processing
-Git version control
Desirable:
-EEG signal processing
-Graph Neural Networks (PyTorch Geometric
or DGL)
-Time-series analysis
-Computer Vision or Human–Computer
Interaction
-GPU programming (CUDA)

Sponsor: (Sisira Adikari)

Brief description:
This capstone project will design a proposed
web-based consultation-booking system for
university students. It adopts a Design Science
approach to apply an accountable translation
framework when developing and evaluating
system-design artefacts. The framework
connects user and stakeholder evidence with
requirements, interface designs, data models,
and technical decisions. It uses artefact
mapping, provenance tracking, and gap-flagging
to maintain inspectable relationships across
design activities. Students will develop and
evaluate a high-fidelity interactive Figma
prototype. They will also produce supporting
requirements, architecture, data, privacy,
security, accessibility, testing, and decision
artefacts. The project sponsor will provide
guidance on applying the framework.

Scope:
 Define the design problem, objectives, and context.
 Review relevant literature and established design
knowledge.
 Collect and analyse requirements from capstone
students and academics, subject to applicable
university requirements.
 Develop user profiles, journey maps, requirements,
user stories, and acceptance criteria.
 Apply the accountable translation framework,
including artefact mapping, provenance tracking, and
gap-flagging.
 Design booking, rescheduling, cancellation, and
confirmation workflows.
 Develop a high-fidelity interactive Figma prototype.
 Develop a conceptual data model, system
architecture, and processing specifications.
 Specify privacy, security, validation, and
accessibility requirements.
 Evaluate the prototype and related system-design
artefacts using feedback from capstone students and
academics, requirements-based checks, accessibility
and usability inspections, and realistic scenarios. All
stakeholder engagement must meet applicable
university requirements.

transformations, responsibilities, unresolved gaps,
limitations, and design-to-engineering relationships.

modelling, project management, teamwork,
and technical communication. Some
familiarity with Figma is desirable, but
students can develop the required
prototyping skills during the project. No

Project ID: 2026-S2-63

Project title: Student-AI Hybrid
Teams: A
Framework for
Validating GenAI’s
Contributions in
Group Work

Sponsor: (Zeena
Alsamarra'i)

Brief description:
Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) has
brought about an unprecedented disruption to
the higher education sector, facilitating
opportunities for personalised learning,
supporting research and writing, and providing
instant clarification and feedback to mention a
few. However, the ubiquity and accessibly to
GenAI services has presented several
challenges, particularly for academic integrity
and increasing reliance on GenAI in
assessments. Higher education institutes have
since responded with several strategies to
facilitate development of AI literacy while
miniating the integrity of our courses and
graduate learning.
In response to GenAI use in assessments, the
University of Canberra has introduced in 2026 a
3-tier system: permitted, guided, or restricted.
Within the ‘guided’ strategy, students are now
encouraged, and in some cases required, to
utilise GenAI tools and services as a resource in
the completion of assessment tasks, but within a
guided framework outlining where and how
GenAI can be used.

Scope:
- Conduct a literature review on the adoption of GenAI
in higher education, with focus on current practices
for validating GenAI content and contributions,
particularly in teamwork.
- Run a short internal survey for how ITS students
validate GenAI content in group assessments.
- Develop a practical GenAI validation framework for
GenAI output validation and associated artefacts that
can be adopted in group assessments while also
maintaining individual team member accountability.
- Time permitting, pilot test the framework in at least
one assessment in unit Corporate Strategy and IT
Governance in S2 2026.

Skill requirements:
- Research skills (ideally completed unit ICT
and Engineering Research Methodology
12090 PG)
- Literature review and writeup
- Survey design skills
- Quantitative analysis skills (statistical
analysis)
- Qualitative analysis skills (thematic
analysis)
- Team management

Project ID: 2026-S2-64

Project title: Beyond Digital

Gradates in the AI
Era

Sponsor: (Zeena
Alsamarra'i)

Brief description:
The mass adoption of Generative Artificial
Intelligence (GenAI) is reshaping the workplace
and setting an increasing expectation for
university graduates to be able to work with
GenAI tools and applications effectively and
ethically. Accordingly, there is now rising
expectation from employers that university
graduates who are digital natives now possess
AI literacy skills as well, a skill set that builds on
digital literacy (ability to create and/or use digital
technologies) but also extend into a capability to
develop and work with AI and GenAI tools and
services, ethically and responsibly. This places
pressure on universities to prepare graduates
who can demonstrate AI literacy skills, at least at
foundational and/or intermediate levels. The
question then is what is AI literacy? How is this
skillset different from digital literacy? Therefore,
this research project aims to investigate these
two skill areas and develop a proposal for
practical strategies that can be implemented by
educators to bridge the gap between the two
within the student’s time at a university.

Scope:
- Conduct a literature review on digital literacy and AI
literacy.
- Develop a matrix that shows the capabilities within
each literacy area.
- Identify the gaps (common areas and new areas
related to use of AI technologies).
- Compile a set of use cases and practices for
university educators (unit conveners and teachers)
who can help students develop this skillset and bridge
the gap between the two.

Skill requirements:
Research skills (ideally completed unit ICT
and Engineering Research Methodology
12090 PG).
Literature review writing and knowledge of
systematic literature review frameworks.
Gap analysis capability.
Visualization skills.
Team management.

Government agencies increasingly rely on digital

enhance future analytical capabilities, but
existing procurement systems are not designed
to accommodate hybrid quantum–classical
approaches. This capstone project adopts a
Design Science approach to design and
evaluate a proposed quantum-ready
government procurement decision support
system. Students will develop a high-fidelity
interactive Figma prototype together with
supporting system-design artefacts using
sponsor-provided documentation and relevant
secondary literature. The project emphasises
transparent, explainable, and quantum-ready
procurement decision support.

Scope:
 Define the design problem, objectives, and
organisational context.
 Review relevant literature and established design
knowledge.
 Analyse the Sponsor Project Initiation Document
and derive functional and non-functional
requirements.
 Design the proposed procurement decision support
system, including its architecture, workflows, data,
and user interactions.
 Develop and evaluate a high-fidelity interactive
Figma prototype together with supporting systemdesign artefacts.
 Incorporate governance, privacy, security,
accessibility, explainability, and quantum-readiness
considerations into the proposed design.
 Evaluate the proposed system design using realistic
procurement scenarios and appropriate analytical
evaluation methods.
 Integrate the developed artefacts into a final report,
presentation, and poster.

Skill requirements:
Skills in business and systems analysis,
requirements analysis, UX design, system
modelling, project management, teamwork,
and technical communication. Some
familiarity with Figma is desirable, but
students can develop the required
prototyping skills during the project. No
advanced programming or quantum
computing skills are required.

Project ID: 2026-S2-67

Project title: Multimodal
Biometric Fusion:
machine Learning
for Iris and
Fingerprint
Authentication

Sponsor: (Xing wang)

Brief description:
This project develops a multimodal biometric
authentication system using a combined kaggle
dataset of iris and fingerprint scans. The dataset
contains high-resolution biometric information
from 45 individuals, comprising 10 iris scans (5
left eye, 5 right eye) and 10 fingerprint scans
(one per finger) per person. Because the data
volume is constrained, students will focus on
few-shot learning and transfer learning
techniques to prevent model overfitting. The
core objective is to extract and fuse the intricate
details of iris patterns and fingerprint ridges to
create a highly robust identity verification system
suitable for high-security access control or
healthcare patient identification.

Scope:
Data Pipeline Engineering: Building multi-input data
loaders that correctly pair an individual's left/right iris
scans with their corresponding fingerprint scans for
unified training.
Feature Extraction: Utilising computer vision
techniques and pre-trained deep learning models
(e.g., ResNet, MobileNet) to extract distinct features
from high-resolution iris images and fingerprint ridge
patterns.
Multimodal Fusion Design: Implementing and
comparing different fusion architectures (such as
feature-level concatenation or decision-level score
fusion) to combine the separate biometric modalities
into a single identity prediction.
Few-Shot Learning & Regularisation: Applying
aggressive data augmentation, transfer learning, or
Siamese network architectures to achieve high
accuracy despite having only 20 total images per
person.

Skill requirements:
Computer Vision & Deep Learning: Strong
proficiency in PyTorch or TensorFlow, with
an understanding of how to implement pretrained Convolutional Neural Networks
(CNNs) for image classification.
Data Science & Statistics: Ability to manage
complex data distributions, handle classmatching logic for multiple inputs, and plot
advanced evaluation curves (e.g., ROC
curves, Equal Error Rate).
Algorithm Optimisation: Understanding of
techniques to combat overfitting on small
datasets, including dropout, batch
normalisation, and advanced image
augmentation strategies.

Project ID: 2026-S2-69

Project title: AI-Enabled
Multilingual Video
Processing and
Social Media
Publishing
Automation

Sponsor: (Ehssan Sakhaee)

Brief description:
This project aims to design and develop an
automated multilingual video processing and
publishing system using n8n and related
technologies. Videos stored in Google Drive will
be processed to generate transcripts and
subtitles, translate captions into selected
languages, prepare appropriate video outputs,
and publish content to selected social media
platforms such as YouTube, Instagram, TikTok
and LinkedIn. Google Sheets will provide a userfriendly interface for configuring, controlling and
monitoring the workflow, including platform and
language selection and publishing status. The
project will investigate free cloud-based and
open-source technologies, with locally hosted
processing used where suitable free cloud
solutions are unavailable.

Scope:
The project includes requirements analysis, system
architecture, development, integration, testing and
documentation of an automated video processing and
publishing pipeline.
High-level activities include:
 Designing modular n8n workflows integrating
Google Drive and Google Sheets.
 Developing a Google Sheets-based control and
monitoring interface for managing videos, languages,
publishing destinations and workflow status.
 Automatically detecting or retrieving videos stored in
designated Google Drive locations.
 Extracting audio and generating timestamped
speech-to-text transcripts.
 Generating subtitle/caption files and translating
captions into multiple user-selected languages.
 Investigating both embedded (“burned-in”) captions
and platform-supported subtitle tracks.
 Processing and formatting video outputs as required
for different publishing platforms.
 Integrating publishing workflows for platforms such
as YouTube, Instagram, TikTok and LinkedIn, subject
to available APIs and platform access.
 Recording processing status, generated files, errors
and published URLs back into Google Sheets.
 Investigating human-in-the-loop review and approval
prior to publication.
 Investigating free cloud, open-source and locally
hosted technologies for transcription, translation and
video processing.
 Implementing appropriate authentication, credential
management, error handling, logging and retry
mechanisms.
 Developing a modular architecture that can be
extended to additional languages, platforms and
content-processing capabilities in the future.
 Producing technical documentation and a handover
package enabling future teams to continue
development.

Skill requirements:
Students would benefit from a combination of
the following skills and interests:
 Workflow automation and n8n
 Systems analysis and requirements
engineering
 Software and API integration
 REST APIs, webhooks and
authentication/OAuth
 Google Drive and Google Sheets
integration
 JavaScript and/or Python
 Video and audio processing, including
FFmpeg
 Speech-to-text and transcription
technologies
 Artificial intelligence and machine learning
 Natural language processing and machine
translation
 Cloud computing and/or local/self-hosted
services
 Database/data management concepts
 Information security and credential
management
 Testing, debugging, logging and error
handling
 Agile software development and project
management
 User experience and human-in-the-loop
workflow design
 Technical documentation and system
architecture
Students are not expected to possess all
these skills at commencement. The project is
particularly suitable for a multidisciplinary
team interested in AI, automation, systems
integration and practical software
engineering.

 1. Key assessment details

 Assessment type: Individual peer evaluation

 Due date and time: 30 October at 23:59

 Points available: 3 points

 Assessment weighting: 3%

 Availability opens: 1 October at 00:00

 Submission method: File upload through Canvas

 Accepted file types: xlsx, xls, pdf, doc and docx

 Required submission: Completed Peer Evaluation Form, including comments

 2. Purpose and learning outcomes

 Peer evaluation supports fairness by reflecting each student's participation and contribution to the group
 project. Project managers must manage and evaluate team members' performance to manage human
 resources efficiently. Group dynamics and working with people with diverse personalities influence project
 outcomes.

 The assessment values both the product and the process equally. The product is the project deliverables
 or report, marked by the supervisor or assessor. The process is how the group worked together and is
 captured largely through peer evaluation to reflect individual contributions accurately.

 Peer evaluation recognises that contributions may differ and gives each team member a say in how marks
 are distributed. It is an opportunity to reflect honestly on both teammates and yourself.

C. Peer Evaluation (Individual) | Assessment requirements 1

Process and mark calculation

 3. How peer evaluation works

 Complete a confidential Peer Evaluation Form containing 10 short questions. Rate yourself and every
 team member on a scale from 0 to 10 for contribution across areas such as communication, effort and
 teamwork.

 Complete one column for yourself and one column for each teammate, using their names. Your Peer
 Evaluation Index (PEI) is the average score you receive from your teammates. The instructions describe
 the PEI used in mark moderation as an average percentage score.

 4. How PEI affects the final group assignment marks

 The final group assignment marks for the Poster, Presentation and Final Report are moderated by the
 PEI. Half of the mark reflects the group result, and half is adjusted using the PEI.

 Final Individual Mark (E) = ((Group Mark) / 2 x PEI) + (Group Mark) / 2

 Use the PEI as a decimal proportion in the calculation, as shown in the supplied example: 90% is entered
 as 0.9.

 Worked example supplied in the instructions

 If the group earns 80 out of 100 and the student's PEI is 90%:

 E = (80 / 2 x 0.9) + (80 / 2)
 E = 36 + 40
 E = 76

 Equivalent formula using E1, E2 and E3

 The instructions also express the combined final group assignment mark as E1 + E2 + E3:

 E = ((E1 + E2 + E3) / 2 x PEI) + ((E1 + E2 + E3) / 2)

 This formula moderates 50% of the combined group assignment mark to recognise both team effort and individual
 contributions. The supplied text does not separately identify which component corresponds to E1, E2 or E3.

 5. Required form and submission

 This formula moderates 50% of the combined group assignment mark to recognise both team effort and individual

 5. Required form and submission

 Read the instructions carefully, complete the designated Peer Evaluation Form and submit it electronically
 via Canvas. The source refers to a downloadable form, but its download URL and the 10 question texts

C. Peer Evaluation (Individual) | Assessment requirements 2

Validity, feedback and rubric

 6. What counts as a valid submission

 To receive the 3% peer evaluation mark and have your feedback count towards teammates' marks, you
 must:

 1. Submit a completed Peer Evaluation Form via Canvas with honest assessments for all team members,
 including yourself. Use a named column for each person.

 2. Give differentiated scores across the 10 items, reflecting strengths, effort and areas for improvement.
 Reflect honestly on your own performance.

 3. Include brief, constructive comments that explain your ratings or provide constructive feedback.
 Comments are required.

 Inflating your own scores or teammates' scores without honest reflection weakens the process and is
 described in the instructions as easy to detect.

 7. Invalid submissions and consequences

 Blank submissions, uniform evaluations (everyone receiving the same assessment scores), and
 submissions missing comments are invalid. Incomplete evaluations, including missing team members,
 receive no marks under the rubric.

 If your submission is invalid, you receive 0% for the peer evaluation component and are excluded from
 your teammates' average PEI calculations.

 8. Tips for fair and constructive feedback

 Do not focus only on who did the most work. The items measure different contributions, including
 organisation, communication, learning and initiative. Give honest, fair scores based on what you observed.
 Use comments to explain key points, especially very high or very low ratings.

 Suggested positive comment starters
 “Bingo consistently stepped up to lead technical aspects of the project…”
 “Jenga communicated clearly in every meeting and helped coordinate our timeline…”

 Full Marks - 3 points: Completed form with differentiated scores and short, constructive comments that

 2. Purpose and overview

 The assessment evaluates the quality of the complete project plan, with clear articulation of business value
 through the content, style and structure of a poster.

 A poster is a visual presentation of the project. It provides a creative opportunity to share project work with
 a broader audience in an interesting and captivating manner.

 The poster should be consistent with and complementary to the oral presentation and project report. It
 should comprehensively cover the motivation, background, problem and rationale, showing how the project
 addressed the sponsor's needs through a combination of pictorial and textual presentations.

Poster (Group) | Assessment requirements 1

Poster preparation requirements

 3. Dimensions and readability

 The required deliverable is a one-page digital academic poster. It should maintain the standard resolution
 for a printed A0 poster, measuring 841 x 1189 mm, and include relevant images such as photos, graphs or
 illustrations.

 A suggested creation method is a PowerPoint presentation with a customised slide size of 841 x 1189 mm.

 Text should be readable from five feet away when printed. Use a minimum font size of 18 points.

 4. Required poster content

 The poster should include the following sections and supporting details:

 1. Title

 2. Executive Summary / Abstract

 3. Background / Introduction / Motivation

 4. Materials / Methods

 5. Results

 6. Key findings

 7. Conclusion

 8. Other relevant details, such as references, footnotes, acknowledgements and sponsors

 5. Design and communication requirements

 1. State the question or problem being addressed clearly.

 2. Focus on the salient aspects of the project and remove unnecessary details.

 3. Use schematic diagrams, graphs, tables and other visual strategies to tell the project story.

 4. Draw the viewer's visual attention rather than explaining the project with excessive text as in a report.

 5. Organise the poster so it generally reads from left to right and from top to bottom.

 6. Properly label, integrate and number visual graphs, pictures and tables in their order.

 7. Cite and reference sources of information other than your own.

 8. Keep the text brief and follow the KISS principle.

 Criterion: Quality and Content of Poster. Maximum: 10 points.

 Poster covers all important topics. Excellent quality through creative and artistic presentation and design.

 Poster covers most important topics. Good quality in the presentation of content. Clear, succinct and

 Poster covers majority of topics. Good quality in the presentation with room for improvement. Clear and

 Poster covers essential topics. Ordinary presentation in the use of graphics, text and design. Requires
